# Otter.ai Public API

17 days ago Updated

Plan required

This content is available for the Otter Enterprise plan and may require admin permissions.

Otter.ai’s Public API provides programmatic access to retrieve channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, and workspace details from your Otter account.

Getting Started: Otter's Public API is available for all Enterprise workspaces. If you do not see this feature for your workspace, contact your Otter account manager.

## API Fundamentals Copy link

Essential information for authenticating, paging through results, and understanding usage limits.

## Authentication Create and manage your API keys Copy link

All API requests require authentication using Bearer token authentication. Follow the steps below to create your API key. 

  1. Go to Integrations → Developer. 
Image
  2. Click Create key.

Image

  3. Click Copy and store the API key in a safe place.

Note: This is only visible once. Make sure you copy the API key in this pop-up. If you forget to copy, follow steps 1-3 to create another key.

Image

  4. The API key can now be used. Follow steps 1-4 to create another API key.

Note: There is a limit of 2 API keys per user.

Image

Using your API key:

Include your API key in the Authorization header for every request:

Example

Copy
    
    `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`

[Button: Show more]

✅ Security best practices:

  * Never share your API key publicly or commit it to version control
  * Store API keys securely using environment variables or secrets management
  * Rotate API keys periodically

## Rate Limits Copy link

Enterprise plan users are currently limited to 10 requests / second. If you exceed your rate limit, you'll receive a `429 Too Many Requests` response.

# REST API

HTTP endpoints for server-side integrations.

The SDK uses these HTTP endpoints under the hood. You can call them directly from your server for backend integrations, async conversion tracking, or non-browser surfaces like native apps and email.

The REST API mirrors what the SDK does on the client. Every call needs your project API key in the request body (the same key that's in your snippet) so we can attribute the call to the right project. The visitor UUID returned by `/sdk/init` is the linking identifier you carry through subsequent calls — including server-side conversion attribution.

For full request and response schemas, parameter types, and a try-it-out console, visit the API Reference page. The summary table below is the quick orientation.

Method  | Endpoint  | Description
--- | --- | ---
POST  | /sdk/init  | Initialize visitor, get test config
POST  | /sdk/track  | Track custom events
POST  | /sdk/convert  | Record conversions
POST  | /sdk/identify  | Send user properties
GET  | /sdk/active/:key  | Verify snippet installation

# Authentication

How your app proves who it is when calling the Otter API — and how you verify that inbound webhooks really came from Otter.

There are two directions:

Direction  | What you do  | Primary mechanism
--- | --- | ---
Outbound — your app → Otter  | Call REST endpoints  | OAuth 2.0 access token as `Authorization: Bearer …`
Inbound — Otter → your app  | Receive webhooks  | Validate `X-HMAC-SHA256` on every request

Exact token request/response fields live in the API reference. Code samples for webhook HMAC live in Keep webhooks secure.

## Application credentialsCopy Anchor Link

Create your application through the gated self-service flow in PartnerHub, or ask your Otter contact for help when that flow is unavailable. After provisioning finishes and you can open the application, select it in Developers and open Keys for its OAuth Client ID and client secret.

Use the Client ID shown on Keys, rather than assuming it is interchangeable with an application identifier.

# Partner Hub

## Overview

Partner Hub is Otter's new workspace for partners who build integrations with Otter's APIs. It's where you set up your integration, get the credentials to connect your systems to Otter, and test everything in a safe sandbox before you go live.

With Partner Hub, you're able to:

  * Create an application for your integration and work in its sandbox workspace
  * Get and manage the API credentials that connect your systems to Otter
  * Set up webhooks so your systems are notified when events happen
  * Test against stores that Otter provisions for you
  * Review your requests, responses, and delivery results in logs, without needing to submit a support ticket
  * See configuration changes made by your team in one place

Partner Hub Login
Partner Hub is currently invitation only. You will receive an email with further instructions to set up your account

### Partner Hub Features 

Partner Hub puts the tools you need to build and test an Otter integration in one place, so you can move faster and troubleshoot on your own.

# About your Otter Business free trial

Otter Help

April 01, 2026 21:04 Updated

When you sign up for a free trial of Otter Business, your team can experience everything that Otter Business offers.

  * Otter Notetaker
  * Otter AI Chat
  * Automated Summaries
  * Automatic sync of audio/video files from Dropbox

Check out the full list of features for the Otter Business plan on our pricing page.

## Start your free trial

To start your Otter Business free trial, navigate to our Get Started for Free page and select the Business Trial. You will be required to enter your payment information, but you will not be charged during the trial period.

Note: A credit card is required to start the Otter Business free trial. Your Workspace will be charged only after the trial period has ended AND you haven't canceled your trial.

## What happens when the trial ends

After your trial period is complete, the card on file you entered during sign-up will automatically be charged for the current number of seats in your Workspace, at the Otter Business monthly rate.
Image

Alternatively, you may cancel the trial anytime before it expires to avoid any charges. To find out when your trial ends, navigate to Account Settings > Plan. 

### Cancel your trial

If you wish to cancel the trial before it expires, follow the steps below:

Note: Only an admin can cancel the trial. Make sure you are signed into an admin account before proceeding. 

  1. Click your profile in the upper corner to expand the menu.
  2. Select Account Settings and click the Plan tab.
  3. Under the Billing Contact section, click Cancel trial.
Image
  4. In the popup, review what will happen when you cancel your trial. Click Cancel trial to proceed.
Image
  5. Your trial is now canceled. Your Workspace will not be charged at the end of the trial period.
